Orchid made her way to the corner of the training grounds, where she had set up several targets reserved for her own use—well, she had never actually said that anyone else was forbidden from using them, but everyone had decided they were hers, if only because the targets were shaped so very distinctively.
She had just come from another headache of an A6 mission debrief. Catapult had gone off on her own again, the report Spot handed in was covered edge to edge with storyboard sketches for his new comic, and Midnight had tried to slide by on a handful of bar coupons. She could feel that familiar exasperation surging in like a tide.
Orchid drew a deep breath, and drew her bow.
What she hunted, as far as she was concerned, was not beasts. It was chaos.
It was plain enough that coming home from the Bubbly Realm had changed nothing whatsoever about her life, and that a shift of heart in one particular moment could not quiet the anger reality kept handing her.
Thwip. The arrow buried itself precisely in Spot's chest. She thought of that slapdash report and that lazy face of his.
Thwip. The arrow tore through Midnight's collar. She thought of that stinging perfume and his whole practiced routine of excuses.
Thwip, thwip, thwip. She thought of the almost self-destructive delight Catapult took in a fight. Her breathing quickened, and the arrows flew one after another until that target bristled with them.
Then her gaze came to rest on the last target. Popukar. Orchid drew her bow and took aim at it.
Popukar had always been the child who gave her the most trouble—because Popukar stubbornly believed that A6 would go on existing forever, and not a bit of that had changed as she grew older.
Sometimes that conviction of Popukar's filled Orchid with the dread that she would be tangled up in A6's troubles for the rest of her life.
But she stood gazing at Popukar for a long while, and in the end she took one deep breath, and was calm.
She had never done anything of the sort before—she would simply lose her temper. But she knew that losing her temper accomplished nothing, that this lot would never change, and that in the end she would have to swallow it alone.
Since coming back from the Bubbly Realm, though, she had decided to try a new approach, and to her surprise the members of A6 had no complaints about it whatsoever. They had even started teasing one another over whether she had put an arrow in this or that person's target today. And for her part, every time she did it, a few thoughts would settle in her mind.
She would not scold Spot. She would set her assessment of his report aside for now, and wait until he could not stand it any longer and came to ask her himself.
She decided to pretend she believed Midnight's nonsense, just to see how he would react if she actually did what he told her to do.
As for Catapult—all right, she had to admit it—she did not actually dislike the Catapult of today. If there truly was anything she could do, perhaps it was only to hone her own skills, so that one day she could stop the girl from doing something dangerous, or... help her? Orchid sighed. She really did not want to admit that she was thinking such things.
And Popukar—oh, what could Popukar possibly have done wrong! She was already turning over designs for Popukar's new outfit.
And thinking all this, she happily lowered her bow.
Yes: once the resentment had been let out, she felt lighter herself.
Little by little, she was coming to believe it—that some things really were not as complicated as she had always thought.
